grf_decision_trace.observed_anchor: Current ClayVM stores String constants but VM call/hostcall arguments remain Int-only; current process bridge maps an Int request ID to pre-admitted tuple[str,...]. Current host_process rejects bytes and embedded NUL at its argv boundary.
grf_decision_trace.hypothesis: Clay must keep Bytes/opaque transport distinct from String/argv semantics and admit process effects through explicit typed conversion rather than implicit Bytes-to-String or shell-text coercion.
grf_decision_trace.strongest_counterhypothesis: A single String-like process argument type is sufficient and opaque byte support can be recovered without semantic loss at the host boundary.
grf_decision_trace.falsifier: Probe Linux exec-style argv with an invalid-UTF8 opaque byte payload and with an embedded NUL, alongside a harmless baseline.

unusual_experiment.name: POSIX_ARGV_OPAQUE_INVALID_UTF8_VS_NUL_BOUNDARY
unusual_experiment.interpretation: The Linux/POSIX argv substrate can transport non-UTF8 bytes except embedded NUL. Therefore canonical Clay Bytes cannot be silently normalized through UTF-8 String, while arbitrary Bytes also cannot be claimed losslessly representable as argv. String/Bytes/argv conversion must be explicit and typed.
